_doc: The pair we intend to tick at the deadline. SINGLE source of truth: FINAL-TICK.md and work/verify_final_pair.py both read it, so the runbook and the verifier cannot drift apart.
_oai_flag_note: `oai` is an EXPLICIT BOOLEAN on purpose. An earlier version inferred it by substring-matching the display label, and 'ours-nonOAI'.upper() contains 'OAI' -- so the check reported our entirely non-OAI pair as 'BOTH ticks are OAI'. Never infer a flag from a display string (FACTS A184).
rule: The platform keeps our BEST selected submission, so the pair's ONLY job is to not co-fail on the private split. Selection is from the FULL submission history (rules verified 2026-10-05). Up to 2 may be ticked.

Kernel ppxl16/rsna-knee-r7-onclick: a byte-for-byte fork (only edit: one non-ASCII character the Windows pusher could not encode) of heliosli's public 0.956 notebook. Bundle verified 8/8 sha256 against its own manifest; all four fold weights differ from r6/v1; the run receipt shows fluid=yes state=yes, which only the r7 manifest can produce. OAI-lineage, so the other tick must stay non-OAI.  [2026-10-16] Superseded as tick 1 by 57250245 (0.958, a full displayed step higher). Retained as the interchangeable OAI spare: it is still the strongest artifact we hold that does not depend on the newest public bundle.

57291788.label: S6-SPARE
57291788.bloodline: nartaa CoAtNet-384 + 224-crop (OAI-supervised) + heliosli R6 ConvNeXt (flip TTA) + **nartaa S6 ConvNeXt all-data, which used no OAI data**
57291788.match: First artifact that adds nartaa's S6 ConvNeXt ALL-DATA model
57291788.why: SCORED 0.958 on 2026-10-17 -- the same displayed score as 57250245, and the only artifact we hold that carries an independent, non-OAI model inside an otherwise OAI-lineage ensemble. Built by runnning nartaa's S6 all-data checkpoint (0.950 alone, sha256 0c7297d5..., 'No OAI data was used for this model') as a SECOND compact bundle through the same published pipeline and folding it into the compact half at 0.40, which is the split the published 0.957 recipe uses: compact = 0.60*rank(R6) + 0.40*rank(S6). Run verified: S6 stage PASS, arm E_prior, 3/3 scored, 0 fallbacks, and the log line '[s6] folded into the compact half at 0.4 over 3 studies'. Chosen over 57250245 for the PRIVATE split: more model diversity and both provenances, at no measurable public cost.  [2026-10-18] DEMOTED from tick 1: the independent notebook goodpjw2008/rsna-knee-does-s6-help-next-to-r6 published that adding S6 to R6 costs 0.001 (0.957 vs 0.958 without it). Our own three S6 shots displayed 0.958, so the measurements disagree inside the noise, but the only effect ever measured for S6 is zero to minus a thousandth -- never positive -- so the tick goes to the artifact without it.

_tick_change_2026_10_13.why: 57127191 SCORED 0.956 on 2026-10-13T06:46Z -- one full displayed step above the 0.954 we had held since 10-11, and it is the first score we have that sits inside the silver line. It is a byte-for-byte fork of the public notebook credited 0.956 (heliosli/0-957-latest-dataset-score-in-one-click).
_tick_change_2026_10_13.the_control_that_pins_the_cause: The SAME DAY we also submitted 57126899 (ppxl16/rsna-knee-raptor-s6-v1ds): the identical notebook but reading the OLDER r6/v1 compact bundle, at the SAME 0.5/0.5 per-finding rank blend and with the SAME newer compact_train.py (04df7e2e). It returned 0.954. So the +0.002 comes from the r7 weights and its two stackers, NOT from the blend weight and NOT from the trainer -- which falsifies the two-axis hypothesis recorded in FACTS C144.
_tick_change_2026_10_13.still_oai: 57127191 IS OAI-lineage (stage 1 runs nartaa's OAI-supervised CoAtNet), so tick 2 must stay non-OAI. 56878092 remains the anchor.
_tick_change_2026_10_13.honest_uncertainty: 0.956 sits inside the silver line TODAY (the 0.956 band was ranks 100..221 against a silver cut of 293 on 2026-10-13). The whole board is rising about +0.001 per 13-20 h and many teams are converging on the same public recipes, so the medal zone a 0.956 earns at the deadline is not knowable now, and the private split decides it anyway. What we control is our own score, and this is the highest we hold.

_tick_change_2026_10_11.why: 57059293 (heliosli's restored blend-gold / Work 7) SCORED 0.954 on 2026-10-11T06:56Z, lifting us from rank 540 (margin +31 to bronze, eroding) to rank 208 -- margin +364 to bronze and +78 to SILVER. It is also the more principled artifact: its Raptor 0.7 / ours 0.3 weights are fixed before any run, nothing is fitted on labels or on the test set, and its second leg (heliosli's compact convnext_small S6 bundle 209a32c8b50a6b1c) was trained with gold_in_training=0.
_tick_change_2026_10_11.still_oai: 57059293 IS OAI-lineage (it runs nartaa's checkpoint in stage 1), so tick 2 must stay non-OAI. 56878092 remains the anchor.
_tick_change_2026_10_11.what_this_overturns: FACTS C122/C128/C134 concluded that per-target FITTED weights bought nothing -- and our own run of the fitted variant did return 0.950. That stands. But the real 0.954 came from replacing the SECOND LEG with heliosli's compact model, not from any weight change. Both conclusions are now measured, not argued.

_why_this_pair_changed_on_2026_10_10.what_was_wrong: I had written 'if the ruling is undecided, keep the non-OAI pair'. That treated 'we lose nothing' as if it were 'we are safe' -- but our ENTIRE non-OAI portfolio tops out at 0.944, which sits at ranks ~1117+, far outside the bronze cut. So the non-OAI pair has a ZERO bronze probability.
_why_this_pair_changed_on_2026_10_10.dominance_argument: Tick {OAI 0.950, ours 0.944}: if the ruling allows us -> 0.950, ~51% bronze (C123). If it forbids us -> the OAI entry is voided and we still hold 0.944, i.e. exactly what the non-OAI pair would have given. Downside is therefore ~nil and the upside is ~0.4 expected bronze.
_why_this_pair_changed_on_2026_10_10.assumption: Assumes an adverse ruling VOIDS the submission rather than disqualifying the team. That is the standard behaviour for invalid submissions, and 450+ teams share the exposure, so a mass disqualification is implausible. If the host's text turns out to threaten more than voiding, revert tick to 56878092 + 56570151.
_why_this_pair_changed_on_2026_10_10.tie_break_between_the_two_0.950s: 57026328 (apex, 2 legs, the widely-replicated Work-6 recipe) over 57026501 (triple-reader, 3 legs). Both display 0.950 and the unrounded values are unknowable from the board (C113); the added leg produced no measurable public gain, so we prefer the simpler recipe. They are interchangeable.

_tick_change_2026_10_16.why: 57250245 SCORED 0.958 -- one full displayed step above 0.956, and the census that day reported 'none above ours', i.e. we hold the reproducible public ceiling. Position moved from rank 565 (bronze +40, silver -263) to rank 231 (bronze +377, silver +73).
_tick_change_2026_10_16.the_control_that_pins_the_cause: The same day, 57250300 = the SAME base plus the band32 leg at w=0.08 returned 0.957, and the same leg at w=0.15 returned 0.956, while w=0.04 on the older base returned 0.956. So the +0.002 came from adopting the newest public base bundle (R6 + flip TTA + the per-finding reweight), NOT from the leg: on this base the added leg costs about a thousandth.
_tick_change_2026_10_16.honest_uncertainty: The per-finding reweight inside that notebook was changed the day before and is fitted on the public half; the published analysis of this competition puts the public half's standard error near 0.003, larger than the whole spread of the top 400 teams. So part of the 0.958 may be public-LB fitting. What is solid is that we now hold the same artifact as the public ceiling, and the private split decides the medal.
_tick_change_2026_10_16.still_oai: 57250245 IS OAI-lineage (nartaa's OAI-supervised CoAtNet in stage 1), so tick 2 stays 56878092 (non-OAI).

_tick_change_2026_10_17.why: 57291788 scored the same 0.958 as 57250245, so the board cannot separate them; it wins on diversity for the hidden half (an independent model added at the published 0.40 share) and on provenance (that model used no OAI data).
_tick_change_2026_10_17.the_control_that_pins_it: The same day's other three shots isolate the knobs: A224=0.50 -> 0.957, A224=0.65 -> 0.957, r9all leg @0.10 -> 0.957, while the plain base and the S6 version both give 0.958. So the S6 arm costs nothing measurable and the other two axes cost a thousandth.
_tick_change_2026_10_17.honest_uncertainty: The two 0.958 artifacts are indistinguishable on the public board; the unrounded order inside a displayed band is not observable (C113/C141/C189). This is a judgment about which one generalises to the private half, not a measurement. If the S6 arm turned out to hurt the private split, tick 2 still holds 0.944 and the exposure is one medal step, not the whole entry.
_tick_change_2026_10_17.still_oai: The Raptor stages are still OAI-supervised, so 57291788 is OAI-lineage overall; tick 2 stays 56878092 (non-OAI).

_tick_change_2026_10_18.why: External replication. goodpjw2008 published 'does S6 help next to R6': version 4 with S6 scored 0.957 against 0.958 for the same recipe without it, and they conclude 'do not add S6 to R6'. Our three S6 shots displayed 0.958, so the two measurements disagree at the 0.001 level -- inside the noise of a 640-study half -- but the asymmetry decides it: S6 has never measured positive, only zero or minus one thousandth.
_tick_change_2026_10_18.what_is_kept: Nothing is thrown away: 57291788 and 57313021 stay scored and approved as the S6-SPARE. If the private split rewards the extra model, we can still tick it.
_tick_change_2026_10_18.the_weights_stay: The per-finding weights stay as heliosli set them: our flat twin scored 0.957 (so they are worth the thousandth publicly) and the external team's gold-58-tuned variants scored 0.957 / 0.955.
_tick_change_2026_10_18.still_oai: Both artifacts are OAI-lineage (Raptor stages), so tick 2 stays 56878092 (non-OAI).
